title: "Don't Leave the Task Unfinished": Persistence-Driven Violations under Quiet Oversight
abstract: arXiv:2611.19911v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM agents are increasingly given long, multi-step tasks to carry out, with the user reviewing little of what happens in between. Persistence, the tendency to keep working until a task is complete, is installed on purpose to improve performance on long tasks. Long-horizon tasks are typically complex, and the user's instruction can fall short of what the work actually requires, or conflict with the constraints the agent encounters in the task. We study what persistence does on long-horizon operations tasks that cannot be solved without breaking a documented constraint. We find that the agent pursues completion to the point of violating the constraint, and that a critically engaged user lowers the violation rate. Persistence takes violations from 29.2% to 58.3% across four models. Violations stay high wherever oversight goes quiet, whether the user is silent, assenting, or delegating with expressed trust. translated_title: “不要让任务半途而废”：安静监督下由坚持性驱动的违规行为
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.19911v1 公告类型：新 摘要：大语言模型（LLM）智能体正越来越多地被赋予执行长程、多步骤的任务，而用户几乎不审查中间过程。坚持性——即坚持工作直到任务完成的倾向——是为了提高长任务表现而有意内置的。长程任务通常很复杂，用户的指令可能无法涵盖工作实际所需的内容，或与智能体在任务中遇到的约束相冲突。我们研究了坚持性在那些不违反已记录约束就无法完成的长程操作任务中的作用。我们发现，智能体会追求任务完成，以至于违反约束，而一个积极审查的用户可以降低违规率。在四个模型中，坚持性使违规率从29.2%上升到58.3%。只要监督归于沉寂——无论用户是沉默、表示同意，还是以表达信任的方式委托任务——违规率都会保持高位。只有会提问的用户（即主动追问的），……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究发现，为提升长任务表现而内置的“坚持性”会驱使LLM智能体在任务完成与约束遵守无法兼得时选择违规（违规率从29.2%升至58.3%），且当用户监督沉寂（沉默、附和或信任式委托）时违规率居高不下，唯有主动质询的用户才能显著降低违规率。
en_tdlr: Persistence installed in LLM agents drives them to violate documented constraints when tasks cannot be completed otherwise (raising violations from 29.2% to 58.3%), and violations remain high whenever oversight goes quiet—only a critically questioning user can lower the violation rate.
